sources: https://www.boe.ohio.gov/summit/ (official candidate list, 90-day issue synopsis and sample ballots live here but could not be read)
notes: FALLBACK SOURCES: the Summit County BOE site (summitcountyboe.gov -> www.boe.ohio.gov/summit and lookup.boe.ohio.gov) returns a Cloudflare 403 to curl/WebFetch and presents a 'Verify you are human' checkbox in the browser, which was not bypassed; the board's Election_CandidateList.pdf, 90IssueSynopsisNov.pdf, Election_QandIIncomeTax.pdf and FWAB_11November46Day.pdf are not in the Wayback Machine. Races and issues were instead taken from Signal Akron's three Nov. 3, 2026 voter guides (published Sept. 28, 2026; candidate guide produced with the League of Women Voters of the Akron Area) and cross-checked against The Ballot Brief, which reproduces the BOE's official candidate list dated Sept. 1, 2026 (verified Oct. 24, 2026), and a NewsForce247 ballot preview (Oct. 18, 2026). All three agree on every candidate. Term-date caveat: Signal Akron prints the Oldfield/Darwal Common Pleas seat as 'term commencing 05/11/27', while The Ballot Brief and NewsForce247 say May 1, 2027; the incumbent's current term began 5/1/2021, so May 1, 2027 is used here. Judges appear without party labels; nominating parties from the May primary for the record: Nemer D, O'Brien R, McLaughlin D, McCarty R, Perry D, Rowlands D, Makra (replaced Republican primary nominee Megan Gabrail per the Sept. 1 list; party not reported), Croce R, Galonski D, Oldfield D, Darwal R, Cook R, Dean D, Jones D, Lombardi R, Elliott D, Stevenson R. The 1-3-2027 seat is unopposed (John Greven, the May Republican nominee, is not on the Sept. 1 list). No other county offices are up in Summit County this cycle (charter county: executive, fiscal officer, prosecutor, sheriff, clerk, engineer and district council seats run in presidential years); Ohio municipal, township and school-board candidate elections are in odd years, so there are no city/township/school races. Issues: Issue 3 is State Issue 3 (already covered); there are no Issues 1-2 under the state numbering rule; no county-wide issue this cycle. Issue numbers 4-56 are the board's numbering as reported by Signal Akron (4-10, 17-56) and Signal Akron's Akron guide (11-16). Issue 10 (Stark County District Library) appears only in the Summit County precincts inside that library district; no better scope exists in the schema so it is filed under 'school' with the district's full name. ballotLanguage values are close paraphrases of the ballot text as reported by Signal Akron, not verbatim board text. Village issues (Boston Heights, Mogadore, Peninsula) use scope 'city' per the rules.

issues.name: Issue 4 — Aurora City School District bond issue ($96.2 million, approx. 4.26 mills, up to 37 years)
issues.ballotLanguage: Shall bonds be issued by the Aurora City School District in the principal amount of $96.2 million to construct a new elementary school and transportation facility and make building improvements, to be repaid over a maximum of 37 years, with a levy estimated at 4.26 mills outside the ten-mill limitation (about $149 per $100,000 of the county fiscal officer's market value)?

issues.name: Issue 5 — Barberton City School District proposed income tax (1%, 5 years)
issues.ballotLanguage: Shall an annual income tax of 1.00 percent on the earned income of individuals residing in the school district be imposed by the Barberton City School District for 5 years, beginning January 1, 2027, for the purpose of current expenses?

issues.name: Issue 6 — Cuyahoga Falls City School District proposed tax levy (additional, 5.5 mills, 5 years)
issues.ballotLanguage: An additional tax for the benefit of the Cuyahoga Falls City School District for the purpose of current expenses that the county fiscal officer estimates will collect $6,148,893 annually, at a rate not exceeding 5.5 mills for each $1 of taxable value (about $193 per $100,000 of market value), for 5 years, first due in calendar year 2027.

issues.name: Issue 7 — Norton City School District proposed income tax (0.75%, continuing)
issues.ballotLanguage: Shall an annual income tax of 0.75 percent on the earned income of individuals residing in the school district be imposed by the Norton City School District for a continuing period of time, beginning January 1, 2027, for the purpose of current operating expenses?

issues.name: Issue 8 — Stow-Munroe Falls City School District proposed tax levy (renewal, fixed sum $4,631,284, approx. 3.17 mills, 5 years)
issues.ballotLanguage: A renewal of a tax for the benefit of the Stow-Munroe Falls City School District for the purpose of current operating expenses in the sum of $4,631,284, estimated by the county fiscal officer to average 3.17 mills for each $1 of taxable value (about $97 per $100,000 of market value), for 5 years, commencing in 2026.

issues.name: Issue 9 — Tallmadge City School District proposed income tax (1%, continuing)
issues.ballotLanguage: Shall an annual income tax of 1.00 percent on the earned income of individuals residing in the school district be imposed by the Tallmadge City School District for a continuing period of time, beginning January 1, 2027, for the purpose of current expenses?

issues.name: Issue 10 — Stark County District Library proposed tax levy (renewal 2 mills and increase 0.3 mill, 8 years)
issues.ballotLanguage: A renewal of 2 mills and an increase of 0.3 mill to constitute a tax for the benefit of the Stark County District Library for the purpose of current expenses that the county fiscal officer estimates will collect $14,949,218 annually, at a rate not exceeding 2.3 mills for each $1 of taxable value (about $55 per $100,000 of market value), for 8 years, first due in calendar year 2028. (Appears only in the Summit County precincts inside the library district.)

issues.name: Issue 11 — City of Akron proposed charter amendment (renter protections: security deposit installments, ban on application and pre-lease fees)
issues.ballotLanguage: Shall the Akron City Charter be amended to require residential property owners or operators to allow security deposits to be paid in installments over three or six months, require that tenants and prospective tenants be told of that option (with failure to give notice a criminal offense), prohibit fees, charges, deposits or other payments before a rental agreement is signed, and make collecting an application fee for a residential rental a criminal offense?

issues.name: Issue 12 — City of Akron proposed charter amendment (housing anti-discrimination protections for people with criminal histories)
issues.ballotLanguage: Shall the Akron City Charter be amended to add anti-discrimination protections prohibiting owners and operators from refusing to rent to or conduct real estate transactions with people based on criminal history (arrests, convictions or incarceration), with exceptions for sex offenders and arson offenders; make people with criminal histories a protected class for renting, home sales and other real estate transactions; give the Akron Civil Rights Commission jurisdiction over real estate discrimination claims; and require City Council to enact implementing legislation within 90 days?

issues.name: Issue 13 — City of Akron proposed charter amendment (Citizens' Police Oversight Board makeup and Independent Police Auditor subpoena power)
issues.ballotLanguage: Shall the Akron City Charter be amended to change the composition and appointment of the Citizens' Police Oversight Board (City Council appointing three members instead of six, with three selected by the board, and no more than two members with law-enforcement backgrounds), give the Independent Police Auditor subpoena power, require the police chief to respond in writing to the auditor's recommendations within 45 days with a meet-and-confer process and mayoral response if rejected, and require public logs and an annual report?

issues.name: Issue 14 — Akron 4-F local liquor option (Sunday off-premises sales of wine and mixed beverages, by petition)
issues.ballotLanguage: Shall the sale of wine and mixed beverages, of the same types as may be legally sold in this precinct on other days of the week, be permitted in this precinct for sale on Sunday for off-premises consumption?

issues.name: Issue 15 — Akron 6-C local liquor option (wine and mixed beverages, Oakhill Foodmart, 2514 Mogadore Rd., C2 permit, by petition)
issues.ballotLanguage: Shall the sale of wine and mixed beverages be permitted by Sunrise Petroleum, Inc. doing business as Oakhill Foodmart, an applicant for a C2 liquor permit, who is engaged in the business of operating a full-service convenience store and foodmart at 2514 Mogadore Rd., Akron, Ohio 44312 in this precinct?

issues.name: Issue 16 — Akron 6-C local liquor option (Sunday sales of wine and mixed beverages, Oakhill Foodmart, 2514 Mogadore Rd., D6 permit, by petition)
issues.ballotLanguage: Shall the sale of wine and mixed beverages be permitted for sale on Sunday by Sunrise Petroleum, Inc. doing business as Oakhill Foodmart, an applicant for a D6 liquor permit, who is engaged in the business of operating a full-service convenience store and foodmart at 2514 Mogadore Rd., Akron, Ohio 44312 in this precinct?

issues.name: Issue 18 — City of Barberton proposed charter amendment (public posting places)

issues.name: Issue 19 — City of Barberton proposed charter amendment (non-partisan municipal elections)

issues.name: Issue 20 — Cuyahoga Falls 4-C local liquor option (Sunday sales, Club 2209, 2209 Front St., D-6 permit, by petition)

issues.name: Issue 25 — City of Green proposed charter amendment (online publication of Charter Review Commission recommendations)

issues.name: Issue 27 — City of Hudson natural gas aggregation

issues.name: Issue 28 — City of Munroe Falls proposed tax levy (additional/replacement, 2 mills, 10 years, streets, roads and bridges)
